emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A numbered Porsche Design Edition 1 (580/777) in black with the stripe package is genuinely desirable. The score is capped until a manual gearbox is confirmed; a Tiptronic would drop it sharply.

A Tiptronic gearbox, cylinder scoring, or high over-rev counts would sharply weaken it.
A price negotiated toward the ~$29k fair-value midpoint would improve value.
Refusal of an independent PPI would end consideration.
evidence.mission_note: As a numbered Edition 1 Cayman S it fits the future-keeper category only. At about $31.5k it sits far above the ideal band and conflicts with cash preservation while in accelerated_bridge mode. The 3.4 S profile requires engine due diligence this listing does not yet supply.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes to a 2008 Cayman S 3.4, a numbered Porsche Design Edition 1 plaque (580/777) is photographed, and an AutoCheck summary reports a clean title, no accidents and three owners. Nothing in the photos shows a visible defect; panels look straight and paint glossy. The transmission is not stated, which is decisive for the enthusiast brief and for value. No maintenance evidence of any kind is offered: no borescope, no DME over-rev report, and no cooling, AOS, clutch or water-pump records, all of which the profile treats as essential for an M97 3.4 S. At $31,545 including fees, the price is roughly 8% above the $29,284 fair-value midpoint and near the top of the range. Comparable sales show 70k-mile S cars between about $30.5k and $34.5k, so the Edition 1 premium is modest. Everything about engine health remains open until an independent specialist inspection is done.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer to confirm the transmission and to agree in writing to an independent Porsche-specialist PPI with borescope and DME over-rev report in the Seattle area before any deposit.
